summary: Gone Hanover County tower listed as Peaks (Lower Hanover). The name matches Peaks Turnout, a 1915 school site, but no source ties the tower to it.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source confirms what remains at the site.

evidence.supports: Hanover County tower at the stated coordinates, status Gone
147-acre Peaks Turnout farm in Hanover County bought in 1914; Virginia Industrial School for Colored Girls opened in 1915 with 28 students
evidence.quote: In 1914, a 147 acre farm at Peaks Turnout in Hanover County was purchased, and in 1915, the Virginia Industrial School for Colored Girls opened with 28 students.

evidence.supports: school became all-male and was renamed the Barrett Learning Center for Boys in 1977
evidence.quote: In 1977, it became all-male and was renamed the Barrett Learning Center for Boys.

evidence.supports: school later became the Barrett Juvenile Correctional Center and closed in 2005
evidence.quote: The school later became the Barrett Juvenile Correctional Center and was closed in 2005.

evidence.supports: video title describing a lookout tower on the grounds of a 1915 abandoned detention center
evidence.quote: Lookout tower on a 1915 abandoned detention center grounds.

sources.title: The Virginia Industrial Home School For Wayward Colored Girls Opens

notes_for_editor: Conflict, unresolved: the association lists this tower as gone, but a YouTube video title describes a lookout tower on the grounds of a 1915 abandoned detention center. Only the title was readable; the video's place, date and identity of the tower are not confirmed, so the name-based link to the Barrett school site is an inference. Do not add the video claim as fact without a register, agency or dated source. Current ownership and public access of the former school land are not established by any source here, and the story advises against entering the grounds. Only four sources; no NHLR or FFLOS register entry was found for this tower.
